text: Berta Singerman Begun (Belarusian: Берта Сінгерман; 9 September 1901 – 10 December 1998), known as Berta Singerman, was an Argentine singer and actress. She was born in Minsk, which was then part of the Russian Empire, into a Jewish family. She emigrated to Argentina with her parents as a child. From an early age, she performed dramatic works with her siblings and neighbors, directing them. At eight years old, she joined a company that produced melodramas in Yiddish, and at ten, she joined a cast performing works by August Strindberg. At fifteen, she married Rubén Enrique Stolek, who became her manager and launched her career in literary declamation. Her associations with prominent literary figures such as poet Alfonsina Storni and writer Horacio Quiroga contributed to her international fame, and she became friends with notable writers and artists including Pablo Neruda, Juan Ramón Jiménez, Gabriela Mistral, and Alejo Carpentier. By the 1930s, Singerman was performing across the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking world, including Spain, Mexico, and Brazil, often drawing large audiences. Her career continued into the 1980s.
